architecture: v2 (re-root after SEND_BACK: winter discharge-to-assess packages across five hospitals)
slot_note: re-root of task127 in the same objective (Opportunity Sizing), wave 1 of sathay3012
niche: an NHS integrated care board dividing its winter discharge fund's discharge-to-assess home-care packages across five acute hospitals by the occupied bed-days each package frees, when a pathway-1 patient's delayed days fuse the wait for home care with the hospital's own take-home medicines and transport
stakeholder_role: the integrated care board's head of system flow, who splits the winter discharge fund's discharge-to-assess packages across the five hospitals

spine.entity: one adult inpatient discharge from one of the five hospitals, with its pathway, admission, medically optimised and discharge times

world.org_type: an NHS integrated care board with a winter discharge fund, five acute hospitals in two trusts, and the county council's home-care brokerage

driver: The decisive quantity is the part of each unit's recorded wait that the offered intervention removes, because the recorded wait fuses the step the intervention replaces with a concurrent step it leaves in place, so only the replaced step's excess over the concurrent one, built by joining separate operational logs, counts; ranking units by the recorded wait, or by the replaced step measured from the same start, credits the units whose concurrent step is slowest.
driver_concrete: A discharge-to-assess package removes only the days a pathway-1 patient spends waiting for home care to start after the hospital's own take-home medicines and transport are ready, so the bed-days it frees are the care start's excess over the later of medical optimisation, medicines and transport, built from the brokerage, pharmacy and transport logs; the national return's delayed days and the care wait counted from medical optimisation both credit the hospital whose own discharge process is slowest.
stump: A competent solver takes last winter's pathway-1 delays (medically optimised to discharge, as the national return and the trusts' records count them) or the home-care wait counted from medical optimisation, ranks the hospitals by the days a package would save and fills the packages down that ranking, so the hospital with the slowest medicines and transport takes the most; the step that lands it there is counting days the patient also spent waiting for take-home medicines and transport, which a package does not remove.
analyst_test: An analyst who cleans the discharge records, joins the brokerage's start dates, reads the scheme and the national return correctly and caps each hospital at its eligible patients still fills the packages by the delayed days or by the care wait counted from medical optimisation, because both look like the days a package saves, and so overloads the hospital whose medicines and transport are slowest.
domain_test: Bed-days freed by a discharge pathway is patient-flow analysis (the counterfactual length of stay when one concurrent discharge dependency is removed, with the others left in place); with another field's nouns there is no pathway-1 patient waiting at once for home care, take-home medicines and transport, no national delayed-discharge return fusing them, and the task stops reading the same.

differentiation.task127: v1 capped rebate slots by a co-op crew's weekly meter-set capacity queueing to year end; here nothing queues: the decisive move is which recorded waiting days a package removes when two discharge dependencies run at once
differentiation.task128: task128 books requests against a budget stated for the whole period and spent per interval; here the cap is a count of packages and the decisive move is the part of each patient's recorded wait that a package removes
differentiation.task119: task119 credits a unit with failed waits it could have shortened because its own beds stood free or held empty for planned work; here no bed is held: the patient's wait for home care runs at the same time as the hospital's own medicines and transport, and only the excess is removable
differentiation.task38: task38 recovers a remediation rule from closed cases; here no rule is recovered: the removable days are built per patient from four operational logs
differentiation.task254: task254 v1 apportions burned area across zones by each event's footprint; here the decomposition is in time, the overlap of two concurrent waits in one patient's stay
differentiation.task36: task36's Osterhout R1 finds a decline in the joint distribution of two flat factors through a computed feasibility margin; here nothing declines: each patient's removable days are the care wait's excess over a concurrent process, built per patient
differentiation.task83: task83 v1 enumerates a population only by re-scoring current records under an archived model; here no model is involved: the population of removable days is cut from each stay by the dates of three discharge dependencies

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many of the period's placeable units a fixed team can finish before the period closes, because each unit counts only once that team performs one last step for it, the team's spare weekly capacity is visible only as the ceiling it held through an earlier unrelated surge, and the decision's own volume, bunched by its filed calendar into weeks no closed period approached, queues the later units past the close; the closed record's lag and an annual capacity check both pass, so the placeable count overstates the in-period total wherever the team is small and the units are many.

layer1: several sources for one picture: the national weekly discharge return, the trusts' inpatient discharge records, the council's home-care brokerage, the pharmacies' take-home medicines log and the patient transport service's bookings, each with its own keys, grain and clock
imperfect keys: NHS numbers on the trust and pharmacy records, the council's person ids on the brokerage with the NHS number partly blank, transport bookings keyed on the hospital number
time and units: a weekly return to Sunday midnight counted in patients on each day, discharge records in date-times, brokerage start dates as dates
genuine overlap: brokerage referrals re-sent after a ward move or a declined offer, ward transfers inside one stay
geographies that do not nest: patients' home neighbourhoods mapped to the county's three council districts and the neighbouring county
